methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.avi -vn output.wav. Add a -map option to choose one audio track.
methods.limits: Needs a local FFmpeg that can decode the AVI's audio.

methods.steps: Run magick render.exr render.jpg.
methods.limits: Needs a build with the OpenEXR library.

methods.steps: Open the EXR, choose File > Export As and save it as a JPEG; set the quality in the dialog.
methods.limits: GIMP supports basic EXR only; layered or multiresolution EXR files are not supported.

methods.steps: Run avifenc -q 80 photo.jpg photo.avif.
methods.limits: The -q option sets quality from 0 to 100.

methods.steps: Open the JPEG, choose File > Export As and save it as AVIF.
methods.limits: AVIF import and export need GIMP 2.10.22 or later.

methods.steps: Run magick photo.jpg photo.avif.
methods.limits: AVIF is listed as readable and writable.

methods.steps: Open the JPEG, choose File > Export As and give the file the .psd extension.
methods.limits: Not all blending modes convert to an exact Photoshop equivalent.

methods.steps: Open the JPEG with File - Open, then choose File - Save as PSD.
methods.limits: Photopea converts every file you open into a PSD document.

methods.steps: Run djxl image.jxl image.png.
methods.limits: The output extension picks the format; an animation writes one numbered file per frame.

methods.steps: Open the JXL, choose File > Export As and save it as PNG.
methods.limits: Stable JPEG XL import needs GIMP 2.10.32 or later.

methods.steps: Run magick image.jxl image.png.
methods.limits: Needs a build with JPEG XL support.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mp2 -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k output.mp3.
methods.limits: Needs a build with the libmp3lame encoder.

methods.steps: Import the MP2 with File > Import > Audio, then choose File > Export Audio and pick MP3 as the format.
methods.limits: MP2 is imported natively; saving a project alone does not create an MP3.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v mjpeg -q:v 5 output.avi.
methods.limits: Differs from this page: no 1920 px or 30 fps limit.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -vn output.wma.
methods.limits: -vn drops the video.

methods.steps: With the FFmpeg library installed, import the MP4, choose File > Export Audio and pick WMA (version2) Files (FFmpeg).
methods.limits: FFmpeg library is required; protected media are not ordinary import sources.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mpeg2 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac output.mp4.
methods.limits: Re-encodes video with libx264 and audio with the AAC encoder; FFmpeg must be built with libx264.

methods.steps: Open the file with the Open button, set the video encoder to Mpeg4 AVC (x264) instead of Copy, set the output format to MP4 Muxer and save.
methods.limits: Encoding is lossy.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.opus -c:a aac -b:a 192k output.m4a.
methods.limits: Writes lossy AAC in M4A.

methods.steps: Run opusdec input.opus output.wav; in Audacity choose File > Import > Audio to open the WAV, then File > Export Audio and M4A(AAC) Files FFmpeg from the Format dropdown.
methods.limits: Two-stage workflow; Audacity needs its optional FFmpeg library for AAC export.
